raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The chart displays the development of trade balances, exports, and imports in millions of US dollars from 2020 to 2023, using a dual-axis line and bar graph format. The x-axis represents time, spanning from 2020 to 2023, with tick marks at yearly intervals. The left y-axis, labeled in millions of US dollars, ranges from 0 to 400 and corresponds to the import and export data, while the right y-axis, also in millions of US dollars, ranges from -200 to 400 and is used for the trade balance (saldo) data. The import data is represented by a solid blue line, starting at approximately 200 million US dollars in 2020, decreasing slightly to around 170 million by mid-2020, then rising to a peak of about 280 million in 2022, followed by a period of fluctuation around 260-280 million until late 2023, where it sharply increases to approximately 340 million. The export data is shown as a solid magenta line, beginning at roughly 130 million US dollars in 2020, decreasing to about 100 million by mid-2020, then gradually increasing to a peak of approximately 180 million in 2022, after which it fluctuates between 160 and 180 million until the end of the period. The trade balance (saldo) is depicted as vertical blue bars, with the values ranging from approximately 110 million to -150 million US dollars, showing a generally stable pattern with a significant negative spike in late 2023, where the balance drops to around -150 million.
